brief: Weekly GS portfolio-strategy piece opens with Q3 earnings season: consensus expects S&P 500 EPS growth of 27% year-on-year, down from 33% in Q2 excluding accounting distortions, with AI infrastructure beneficiaries generating more than half of this quarter's growth, so growth is strong but concentrated. GS's US team still expects companies to beat consensus again, helped by strong economic data and positive revision breadth, even as median-stock EPS growth slows from 14% to 9%; most hyperscalers report in October's final week, by which point about 70% of S&P 500 market cap will have reported. Europe also looks positioned for a solid season: consensus expects 23% EPS growth (16% excluding commodities), helped by revision momentum, improving PMIs and euro weakness, pointing to in-line or modestly better results. Weekly recap: global equities rose 0.6%, copper gained 2.5% and Brent 2.1%; Energy and Defensives led, Industrials lagged; the S&P 500 hit a fresh all-time high (+14% YTD) and STOXX Europe is up 7% despite the energy and rates shock. GS's forecast table puts the S&P 500 at 8700, the 10-year UST yield at 4.4%, Brent at $75 and gold at $5235, all 12 months out.
